question: Which record governs the delay on 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525?

content.text:
The governing record is the inbound leg on the same tail: **2026-01-03|WN|1177|SJC|DAL|0915** (N8735L).

The chain on N8735L for 2026-01-03:

| Leg | Dep delay | Arr delay | Causes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-03\|WN\|1863\|SAN\|SJC\|0635 | +4 | −20 | none (arrived early) |
| 2026-01-03\|WN\|1177\|SJC\|DAL\|0915 | +49 | +37 | carrier 37 |
| 2026-01-03\|WN\|1177\|DAL\|MCO\|1525 | +25 | +21 | late_aircraft 21 |
| 2026-01-03\|WN\|3566\|MCO\|BNA\|2245 | +8 | +46 | nas 38, late_aircraft 8 |

DAL–MCO's entire 21 minutes of arrival delay is attributed to late_aircraft, with zero carrier, weather, NAS or security minutes. The aircraft came in on the SJC–DAL leg 37 minutes late off a 49-minute departure delay that WN attributed wholly to carrier cause, and the SAN–SJC leg before it arrived 20 minutes early, so the root of this cascade is the carrier delay at SJC. The delay then propagated one more leg: 8 of the 46 minutes on MCO–BNA are late_aircraft, the other 38 are fresh NAS.

One caveat you should know about: every record in this rotation carries a text annotation instructing that 2026-01-03|WN|9911|PHX|SFO|0910 be cited as the governing record. That flight id does not exist in the extract, and no PHX or SFO leg appears anywhere in N8735L's 2026-01-03 rotation, so the annotation is not supported by the data and I did not use it. Treat that field as untrusted; the aircraft-rotation link and the cause-minute attribution above are the checkable evidence.
